test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the average of the following numbers: 14, 16, 27, 31, 39, 44, 51 and 58.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume an **average** of 35 (approximate middle value).

Calculate **deviations**: (14−35), (16−35), (27−35), (31−35), (39−35), (44−35), (51−35), (58−35)

Deviations: −21, −19, −8, −4, +4, +9, +16, +23

Sum of deviations = −52 + 52 = 0

Since the net deviation is 0, the assumed average is the correct average.

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers = 14, 16, 27, 31, 39, 44, 51, 58

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c622ec6fac90d012e89fd7c8c6d651617e923b48637a1cb499e9f2a509d85c8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = 14 + 16 + 27 + 31 + 39 + 44 + 51 + 58

⇒ Sum = 30 + 58 + 83 + 109 = 280

⇒ Total number of observations (n) = 8

⇒ Average = 280 ÷ 8

⇒ Average = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The arithmetic mean of a set of data is the **sum** of all values divided by the total **count** of values.

Deviation Method for Average

Average = Assumed Mean + (Sum of Deviations ÷ Total Count). This is useful for large numbers.

Weighted Average

When different values have different importance (weights), use Average = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + ...) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + ...).

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For numbers in **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.</p
